title: Inventory multilingual plotting frontends
objective: Generate and validate the current Wolfram and MATLAB plotting syntax/runtime surface, classify implemented and emerging operations, and produce the pinned frontend-surface artifact

oracles: Parser/runtime export inventories and focused generated-artifact tests

handoff.summary: Added a deterministic schema-v1 multilingual plotting inventory generated from the actual Wolfram and MATLAB lowerers, runtime adapters, persistent-session contract, and existing graphics evidence. The 105 records classify 57 Wolfram translations and 20 explicit Wolfram gaps, plus MATLAB's exact plot(x,y) translation and 27 unsupported/emerging state, syntax, plotting, layout, and handle operations. Generic call grammar recognition is kept separate from plotting-specific lowering so unsupported names are never advertised as working. The generated artifact hashes every source input and --check fails on drift.
risks: The artifact is exhaustive for current explicit plotting lowerers/runtime mappings and the plan's first target catalog, but it is not an exhaustive inventory of every plotting name in the full proprietary Wolfram or MATLAB products.

The full pnpm test:integration receipt ran 404 tests and failed 233 because this lightweight worktree has no optional FLINT/FFLAS/igraph/m4ri addons or production kernels; graphics and polyglot kernel tests consequently fail during native package loading before exercising this source-only inventory.

test/plotting-frontend-surface.cjs is intentionally not registered in the shared test/node-test-manifest.cjs because that central file is outside this lane's claim; test:changed therefore also reports the expected manifest gap.
next_steps: Integration lane: register test/plotting-frontend-surface.cjs in the unit runner tier alongside the other plotting tests.
Coverage classifier: consume grammar_recognized, plotting_lowerer_recognized, support_state, and evidence fields rather than treating every parsed call as support.
MATLAB implementation priority: introduce figure/axes state and handles, then LineSpec, hold/grid, labels/limits/legend, scatter, surf/mesh, and layouts.
Wolfram implementation priority: add legends/themes and Prolog/Epilog with explicit option handling, then charts, logarithmic plots, list fields, and remaining 3D regions/streams.
